headline: Aquino Bridge in Tarlac Closed After Portion Collapses in Habagat Rains
seoTitle: Aquino Bridge in Tarlac Closed After Collapse | FMB News
seoDescription: A section of the Aquino Bridge in Tarlac City collapsed before midnight on August 28 after heavy Habagat rains and strong Tarlac River currents, forcing a full closure.
deck: DPWH closed the damaged bridge after strong river currents and persistent monsoon rains caused structural damage late Friday night.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: A portion of the Aquino Bridge in Tarlac City collapsed at about 11:56 p.m. on Friday, August 28, after continuous Habagat rains and strong currents in the Tarlac River damaged the structure.
The timing corrects the approved newsroom brief, which described the collapse as a Saturday event. DPWH inspected the bridge shortly after midnight and kept it closed to vehicular traffic.

sections.heading: Traffic and safety
paragraphs: Barricades were installed and traffic restrictions were imposed near the Molave Y-junction in Barangay San Isidro. Authorities advised motorists to use alternative routes while structural assessment and repair planning continue.

sections.heading: DPWH response
paragraphs: The DPWH Tarlac 1st District Engineering Office said incessant rain and strong river flow damaged the decades-old bridge. Engineers continued assessing the structure and studying immediate repair options.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The collapse occurred during prolonged monsoon rainfall across Central Luzon, when swollen waterways and strong currents were placing added stress on roads, bridges and riverbank infrastructure.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A bridge closure can quickly become an economic and safety problem because it reroutes commuters, freight and emergency access while raising questions about how older river crossings are assessed under more intense rainfall and flooding conditions.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for DPWH repair timelines, updated detour instructions and structural assessments of other river crossings affected by the same weather system.
